name: Pipeline widget
summary: A widget that shows the pipeline engine at a glance: a row of status squares, one per plugin, with the detail on hover, the status line beside them, what is running now and the queue, and a chart of recent runs (name, area, run time, how long ago, runs).
description: It is global only, off the surface until you place it, and it draws the new engine. Hovering a square, focusing it with the keyboard or tapping it opens its detail: how many files wait and how old the oldest is, when it last delivered, its last error and how many are failing, and how many runs since the server started. The overall status line (caught up, behind, stalled, rebuilding or off) sits small beside the row. The engine announces a delivery when it starts as well as when the batch ends, so running shows without polling. A failed run wears a diamond mark, a parked one a dash. Every figure column keeps the room its widest value needs, so the run time is never cut off; the name and area give way first, and a very narrow widget drops the runs and then the area before any figure. The server keeps these rows in memory only (about 100, empty after a restart); it records and logs, it never alerts. Every view shares one read of GET /api/v1/pipeline/status, pushed on the pipeline topic after every batch, park, scan pass and rebuild, so nothing polls while the live connection is up (a 10 second poll runs only while it is down). The developer widget carries it as its pipeline tab. While the conversation backups plugin is on, the chart also shows a backups row (area conversations, #1807): its 30 minute passes plus the captures on close, sleep, restart, clear and fork as runs, the last run's time and duration, and a failed mark when the latest pass or capture failed; with the plugin off the row is not there. It comes through a plugin seam (src/cplugs/sdk/pipeline_rows.py), so the plugin stays self contained.
where: Home screen once added: a cell titled pipeline with a database mark.
The drawer's widget area, once added.
how_to: Open the edit layout control at the bottom of the drawer.
Search widgets for pipeline; press the card to put it on the home page, or press the one under drawer area to put it in the drawer.
Read the status squares and the line beside them, then the chart below: one row per session (or project, or machine) and plugin.
Read running for what the engine is delivering now and queue for what waits next.
Hover or focus a square to see its backlog, last delivery, last error and runs.
To rebuild a plugin, open Settings, pipeline and press rebuild beside it.
examples: See at a glance which plugin is behind or failing by the shape of its square.
See at once whether deep search is behind and by how many files.
See which session the stats plugin last read, how long it took and how long ago.
See that eleven transcripts wait after a restart, and which plugin a failing one waits on.
media_exempt: A widget whose screenshots are captured before the next version bump.
